title: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Its Postulates
topicTitle: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Its Postulates
notes: The kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the physical behaviour of gases (pressure, volume, temperature) in terms of the motion of their molecules. It treats a gas as a large collection of tiny, rapidly moving particles in constant random motion.
Postulates of the Kinetic Theory of Gases
1. A gas consists of a very large number of tiny particles (molecules) which are identical in mass and size for a given gas.
2. The volume of the individual gas molecules is negligible compared to the total volume occupied by the gas. The molecules are point masses.
3. The molecules are in a state of continuous, rapid, random motion in all directions. Between collisions they move in straight lines.
4. The molecules exert no attractive or repulsive forces on one another except during collisions. Between collisions they move freely.
5. Collisions between molecules and with the walls of the container are perfectly elastic — kinetic energy and momentum are conserved, though individual molecular speeds may change.
6. The duration of a collision is negligible compared to the time between collisions.
7. The pressure of a gas is caused by the bombardment of the container walls by the molecules. The force per unit area exerted on the walls is the pressure.

8. The average kinetic energy of the gas molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas: $KE_{avg} = \frac{3}{2}kT$, where $k$ is Boltzmann's constant. At the same temperature, all gases have the same average kinetic energy per molecule.
